# UC-395 — Open a Support Ticket About a Payout or Payment Issue

## Header Info
- **Use Case ID:** UC-395
- **Title:** Open a Support Ticket About a Payout or Payment Issue
- **Actor:** Vendor (ACT-02) — Owner/Editor/Manager staff
- **Trigger:** The vendor hits a payout or payment problem the panel cannot resolve (UC-387, UC-388)
- **Priority:** P2
- **Goal:** Get a tracked, idempotent ticket into the support queue with the payment context attached.
- **Preconditions:** Authenticated session; ticket endpoint available (`POST /support/tickets`, API-ADM-035); attachments obey upload limits (SEC-REQ-011).

## Main Scenario
1. Vendor opens Support → client `POST /support/tickets` with `{ category, subject, body, orderId?, attachmentFileIds? }` and an `Idempotency-Key` (API-ADM-035).
2. Server validates the payload, scans attachments and creates the ticket → `201 { ticketId, status: "OPEN", number: "SUP-000123" }` (API-ADM-035).
3. A duplicate submission with the same key returns the original ticket — exactly one row is ever created (BR-PLT-03).
4. The ticket lands in the support queue for Admin/Moderator triage (`GET /admin/tickets`, API-ADM-039).
5. Vendor tracks it → client `GET /support/tickets` (own tickets only, cursor feed) and replies → `POST /support/tickets/{id}/messages` (API-ADM-036, API-ADM-038).
6. Support resolves with a resolution note → `IN_PROGRESS` on first reply, `RESOLVED` at the end; the vendor may reopen once (API-ADM-041).

## Alternative Scenarios
- **A1 — Link the affected order:** `orderId` attaches the order timeline to the thread for faster diagnosis (API-ADM-035, API-ADM-037).
- **A2 — Attach proof:** ledger reference or payout receipt uploaded as `attachmentFileIds` under the shared upload rules (SEC-REQ-011).
- **A3 — Wrong category first:** the ticket stays open and Admin reassigns it — status moves `OPEN → IN_PROGRESS` on claim (API-ADM-040).

## Exception Scenarios
- **E1 — Missing idempotency key:** → `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`; no ticket is written (BR-PLT-03).
- **E2 — Attachment fails scanning:** → `FILE_SCAN_FAILED`; the ticket is not created (API-ADM-035, SEC-REQ-011).
- **E3 — Reply on a resolved/closed ticket:** → `TICKET_STATE_CONFLICT`; use the reopen path instead (API-ADM-038).
- **E4 — Foreign ticket id:** → 404 `NOT_FOUND`; threads are visible only to opener and support (DATA-REQ-008).

## Postconditions
- Success: one `OPEN` ticket with a `SUP-` number exists, visible to its opener and support staff only (DATA-REQ-008).
- Failure: no ticket row, no orphan attachments — the rejection leaves nothing behind (API-ADM-035).

## Business Rules Applied
- BR-PLT-03, BR-PLT-06

## Related Requirements
- FR-020 (Platform Administration, Settings & Audit)
- Cross-reference: UC-387 and UC-388 are the payout investigations that end here; UC-204 opens an order-scoped ticket.

## Permissions / Data / External Dependencies
- **Permissions:** any authenticated user opens and reads own tickets; Admin/Moderator work the queue (SEC-REQ-004).
- **Data involved:** ticket rows (`status`, `category`, `number`), message thread, attachment files, linked `orderId`.
- **External dependencies:** support queue and assignment (B13); file scanning (SEC-REQ-011); audit entries on assign/resolve (BR-PLT-06).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC-UC395-01:** Given a valid payout-issue payload with a key, when posted, then `201` returns a `SUP-` numbered `OPEN` ticket (API-ADM-035).
- **AC-UC395-02:** Given the same idempotency key replayed, when posted again, then the original ticket is returned — no second row (BR-PLT-03).
- **AC-UC395-03:** Given a failed attachment scan, when posted, then `FILE_SCAN_FAILED` is returned and no ticket exists (API-ADM-035).
- **AC-UC395-04:** Given another user's ticket id, when read, then 404 `NOT_FOUND` is returned (DATA-REQ-008).
